subject: Credit settlement proposal + 30-day pilot extension for CloudYard
messages:
From: Ellie Roberts <ellie@cloudyard.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: trial extension + credit settlement approach

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the quick onboarding help — the pilot is proving useful but we burned through the allocated tokens earlier than expected. Would you be able to:  

- Extend the pilot for 30 days so our infra team can finish the integration tests; and
- Provide a $3,000 promotional credit to cover the overage during the probe so we don’t have an unexpected invoice this month.

For our accounting team, could you confirm how Redwood will record that credit? Ideally CloudYard needs either a credit memo applied to the invoice or a credit on our account (to be netted against the next invoice) so our AP can match to the PO (attached). Also flag any tax implications we should be aware of.

PO attached: CloudYard_PO_4578.pdf

Appreciate your help — Ellie
Ellie Roberts
Head of Platform Integrations | CloudYard
ellie@cloudyard.com
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 08:04:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: trial extension + credit settlement approach

Looping you both in — Customer (CloudYard) is asking for a 30-day pilot extension and a $3,000 promo credit to cover overages. They included a PO; they want something that AP can match to avoid a manual journal on their side.

Questions for finance/billing:  
1) Do we issue a formal credit memo referencing an invoice (there is not an issued invoice yet for this pilot month), or record a pro forma credit and leave it on the customer account as a balance?
2) What GL accounts should we use for the credit (contra-revenue vs marketing/promo expense)?
3) Any VAT/sales tax treatment I should call out to the customer (they're US-based, no VAT)?

I attached a draft credit memo for quick review. Propose we:  
- Approve a $3,000 credit memo on account that will be applied to the first paid invoice post-pilot; and
- Extend the pilot 30 days effective immediately after approval.

If you can reply with preferred accounting path and quick sign-off, I’ll confirm with Ellie.

Thanks,
Sofia
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: trial extension + credit settlement approach

Sofia / Laura —

Short answer: we can do a credit-on-account and hold it as a customer balance (recommended) OR issue a credit memo if there's an invoice to be adjusted. Since Ellie indicated there is no invoice yet, creating a credit memo that sits unapplied is fine and common. Operational notes:  

- Accounting treatment: treat promotional credits as contra-revenue (not an operating expense) to preserve gross revenue reporting. Use GL mapping: Revenue (4000 series) reduced by contra-revenue account 4095 (Promotional Allowances).  
- If the pilot was a true service delivery (we delivered compute/token consumption), and revenue was previously recognized, a correcting journal might be needed. In this case the pilot is ongoing and revenue recognition doesn't apply yet — so simply record a credit memo that reduces future billed revenue.  
- AR mechanics: create Credit Memo CM-2027-0595 in NetSuite, apply to the next invoice when generated, or leave unapplied as a credit balance on the customer. Include PO number on the CM (CloudYard_PO_4578).  
- Tax: US customer — no VAT; review state sales tax only if we were charging taxable services (rare for our model). Billing should capture jurisdiction if needed.  

Laura: please confirm the NetSuite CM flow and GLs, and whether we need a supporting journal for month-end.

Marcus
Director, Finance Operations
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 13:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: trial extension + credit settlement approach

Confirmed — billing can issue CM-2027-0595 for $3,000 and tag it as "Promotional Credit - Pilot Overages". Operational checklist:  

- Attach CloudYard_PO_4578 to the CM.
- Use GL: 4095 (Promo Allowances) for the credit amount; revenue invoices will reference 4001 etc.
- Leave CM unapplied if there is no open invoice; it will appear as credit balance on the customer account. If the customer requests an invoice offset now, we can retro-apply but prefer to leave unapplied to avoid post-recognition adjustments.
- For month-end close (May 31), finance will ensure contra-revenue flow is reflected; no special journal entry needed beyond CM unless revenue had been recognized earlier.

I will create CM-2027-0595 by EOD and add the attachment. Tessa, please confirm the pilot extension in the console once CM is in place.

Thanks,
Laura
Billing Manager
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Ellie Roberts <ellie@cloudyard.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: trial extension + credit settlement approach

Ellie — quick update and next steps:  

Thanks for the PO. We've approved a $3,000 promotional credit and the billing team will issue Credit Memo CM-2027-0595 (Promotional Credit - Pilot Overages) and attach the PO. The credit will be left unapplied on CloudYard’s account and can be used against the next paid invoice; if you prefer it applied to a specific invoice once it's generated, let us know and we can do that.

We’ve also extended the pilot for 30 days effective immediately in the console (Tessa confirmed). No VAT for US-based CloudYard; billing noted no additional tax action required.

Attachments: CY_Proposed_CreditMemo_3000.pdf (draft), CloudYard_PO_4578.pdf

If this works, I’ll close the loop.

Best,
Sofia
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
